title: Metrics Normalization & Trace Enrichment Canvas
content:
Purpose:
This is a working canvas to converge on a repeatable approach for: normalizing raw inference metrics across tenants and models; enriching traces with a compact set of high-value context fields; and prioritizing dashboard widgets that operators actually use during latency/cost incidents. Goal is a minimally invasive rollout that reduces alert noise, enables cross-tenant comparisons, and keeps query cost bounded.

Summary of problems we've seen:
- Percentiles are noisy across tenants with different prompt lengths and model mixes (example: P95 token-latency meaningless for high-prompt tenants).
- Dashboards mix raw counters and derived rates; operators spend time reconciling denominators.
- Traces lack a small set of canonical labels that make automated grouping reliable (session id vs request id vs user id).
- Sampling is currently static and either misses rare slow-path (kv-eviction) traces or floods retention tier.
- Alert fatigue from naively alerting on raw p95 without normalization for prompt-length or token-count.

Design principles (scorecard):
1) Comparability: metrics should be comparable across tenants by normalizing for token_count and model_family.
2) Low-cardinality canonical keys: enrich traces with a small, stable set of attributes for grouping; avoid free-text prompts in labels.
3) Cost-bounded telemetry: prefer derived rates and histograms that compress well; sample traces adaptively.
4) Operator-first widgets: surface the investigator's top 8 panels (latency by slice, kv-heatmap, recent fallback rate, tenant cost spike).
5) Incremental rollout: instrument flags + shadow queries + canary dashboards.

Proposed metric family definitions (naming convention: rhd_<area>_<name>):
- rhd_inference_token_ms.sum: cumulative token processing time (ms). Unit: milliseconds. Ingest: counter.
- rhd_inference_token_count.sum: cumulative tokens emitted/consumed. Unit: tokens.
- rhd_inference_token_ms_per_token.gauge: derived = token_ms.sum / token_count.sum over a consistent window. Unit: ms/token. Use for normalized latency comparisons.
- rhd_request_prompt_tokens.gauge: tokens in prompt (not generated). Use to slice prefill vs generation.
- rhd_kv_cache_hit.count and rhd_kv_cache_miss.count: discrete counters for quick computed hit ratio.
- rhd_prefix_cache_warmth.index: small integer [0..3] categorizing warmness (0 cold, 3 hot) produced by agent runtime.
- rhd_fallback_rate.rate: fraction of requests falling back to cheaper/safer model variant; windowed rate.
- rhd_model_variant.tag: dimension label (small cardinality - e.g., gptx-8q, llama-70b-4bit).

Derivation examples (stored as dashboards/alerts, not raw ingestion where possible):
- normalized_latency_p95_by_tenant = quantile(rhd_inference_token_ms_per_token{tenant=T}, 0.95)
- kv_hit_rate = sum(rhd_kv_cache_hit.count) / (sum(rhd_kv_cache_hit.count) + sum(rhd_kv_cache_miss.count))
- cost_per_token_est = (instance_gpu_hour_cost * gpu_time_ms) / token_count (approx calculation surfaced for ops).

Trace enrichment: canonical fields to attach (keep low cardinality + stable values):
- trace.tags.session_stable_id (hashed, 64-bit) - used to stitch multi-call user journeys.
- trace.tags.prompt_bucket (small enum: short|medium|long) - derived from rhd_request_prompt_tokens thresholds (<=64, 65-512, >512).
- trace.tags.model_family (string): e.g., opt, llama, redwood-ozone.
- trace.tags.model_variant (string): up to 64 unique values; enforced whitelist.
- trace.tags.kv_warmth (0..3): see prefix_cache_warmth.index mapping.
- trace.tags.fallback_path (none|policy|capacity|error) - why fallback happened.
- trace.tags.operator_campaign (optional) - used for A/B/rollouts; defaults to none.

Sampling policy (adaptive multi-tier):
- baseline: keep 1% of all traces per tenant across all requests (to maintain aggregate signal).
- event-driven boost: if normalized_latency_p95_by_tenant crosses threshold, switch that tenant to 100% tracing for 3 minutes.
- rare-path capture: always sample 100% when evicted_from_kv_cache OR fallback_path != none OR model_variant changes mid-request.
- headroom capping: global trace retention quota applied; if retention forecast > cap, reduce baseline to 0.2% for non-high-tier tenants.

Dashboard prioritization rubric (useful for trimming panels):
- Investigability: does the panel point to a next actionable drilldown? (score 0-3)
- Cost per query: expected Prom/ES cost of the query (low/medium/high).
- Operator demand: how often ops used it in last 30 days.
- Fatigue impact: does it reduce alert noise?
Pick top panels with Investigability >=2 and Cost <= medium.

Proposed operator panel set (compact 8):
1) Tenant normalized latency heatmap: tenants x prompt_bucket, cells = p95(rhd_inference_token_ms_per_token).
2) Token flow histogram: distribution of rhd_request_prompt_tokens and generated tokens.
3) KV warmth vs latency scatter: show rhd_prefix_cache_warmth vs token_ms_per_token for slow tails.
4) Hot tenant list (live): tenants with >2x baseline normalized latency or cost-per-token spike.
5) Recent fallbacks table: last 100 requests with fallback_path, model_variant, tenant, brief trace link.
6) Model variant rollout watch: rollout % vs normalized latency delta by cohort.
7) Synthetic probe overlay: expected latency (canary) vs observed per-region.
8) Alert pulseboard: open alerts, suppressed alerts, and noise index (alerts/day/tenant).

Alerting & thresholds (examples):
- Alert: tenant_normalized_latency_breach
  - Expr: normalized_latency_p95_by_tenant{tenant=T} > baseline_p95_by_model_and_bucket * 1.6 for 5m
  - Severity: page if tenant tier == enterprise, else pager-duty email for lower tiers.
  - Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/OBS-RR-2026

Rollout plan (phases):
Phase 0 (week 0): review and align. Mark instrumentation points in runtime agent and define model_variant whitelist. Feature flag for trace enrichment off by default.
Phase 1 (week 1-3): emit new counters (token_ms.sum, token_count.sum, kv_hit/miss, prefix_cache_warmth.index) behind feature flag. Create canary dashboard for internal test tenant.
Phase 2 (week 4-6): enable normalized derived metrics in dashboards (not stored as new time series yet) and enable adaptive sampling for canary tenant. Run 2-week shadow run and collect retention forecast.
Phase 3 (week 7-10): expand adaptive sampling to 10% baseline across production tenants, enable fallback-always-sampling rule. Add alert rules for normalized_latency_breach with conservative thresholds.
Phase 4 (week 11+): full rollout with retention monitoring, query-cost budgets, and ops training session.

Backstop questions & open decisions:
- What exact prompt_token thresholds define prompt_bucket? (proposal: 64/512) - ACTION: decide by 2026-03-10.
- Do we materialize rhd_inference_token_ms_per_token as a raw timeseries or compute at query time? Tradeoff: storage vs query cost. Recommendation: compute at query time for first 6 weeks, revisit.
- Model variant label cardinality limit: what is the allowed max distinct model_variant per cluster? (proposal: 64) - ACTION: ops + model-onboarding to agree.

Implementation notes for runtime engineers:
- Emit rhd_inference_token_ms as a per-token timer aggregated at the runtime boundary to avoid double counting across microcalls.
- Ensure prefix_cache_warmth is a tiny enum produced by runtime heuristics at request end. Avoid embedding large lists in enrichment fields.
- Tagging: runtime should never attach raw prompt text to span tags; instead attach prompt_hash only when needed and never in metrics labels.

Example queries (PromQL-like / pseudo):
- normalized_latency_p95_by_tenant:
  - quantile_over_time(0.95, rate(rhd_inference_token_ms.sum[5m]) / rate(rhd_inference_token_count.sum[5m])) by (tenant, prompt_bucket)
- kv_hit_rate_by_tenant:
  - sum(rate(rhd_kv_cache_hit.count[5m])) by (tenant) / sum(rate(rhd_kv_cache_hit.count[5m]) + rate(rhd_kv_cache_miss.count[5m])) by (tenant)

Ops onboarding checklist (short):
- [ ] Run the canary dashboard walkthrough with SRE + Solutions Eng.
- [ ] Validate kV warmth mapping on 3 workloads (chat assistant, summarization, reranker).
- [ ] Train on new alert semantics and suppression rules.
- [ ] Add one synthetic probe per region and compare to normalized_latency baseline.

Action items (owners & tentative dates):
- Decide prompt_bucket thresholds — owner: Meng Zhao — due 2026-03-10.
- Runtime instrumentation PR for token_ms/token_count + prefix_warmth — owner: Liam O'Connor — PR target 2026-03-01.
- Adaptive sampling scheduler prototype — owner: Sofia Alvarez — prototype 2026-03-08.
- Dashboard canary + alert rules draft — owner: Priya Nair — 2026-03-05.

Notes to self: keep the initial trace enrichment minimal; most value is from a few high-quality labels. When in doubt, prefer fewer labels and richer metric derivations. This doc will be iterated after the first two weeks of the canary run.

References and related docs:
- See ENG-7842 for previous sampling experiments (linked above).
- Runtime agent tagging convention: https://github.com/redwood-inference/agent-spec/blob/main/tagging.md
- Cost forecast spreadsheet (sheet id): SHEET-obs-cost-2026

End of canvas - comments welcome.
